I thought I'd compile some resources for anyone who's interested in learning the lingua Latina. It's a challenging but incredibly rewarding experience.

First and foremost: Wheelock's Latin

I know grammar isn't everyone's idea of fun, but grammar is incredibly important in language, and especially Latin. Wheelock may seem dry at times, but it has almost instant gratification, as the Sententiae Antiquae at the end of each chapter enables you use the skills you learned to translate Latin sentences, even as early as the first chapter.

Exemplī grātiā: agō, agere, ēgī, āctus: (3rd conjugation) do, act; drive, lead; negotiate; spend (life or time). All of these definitions come up pretty regularly. Take your time but learn them thoroughly.
